identity.title: Arp 220: New Observational Insights into the Structure and Kinematics of the Nuclear Molecular Disks and Surrounding Gas

paper_type_evidence.quote: ALMA cycle 3 observations of $^{12}$CO $J = 3\rightarrow2$, $^{13}$CO $J =  4\rightarrow 3$, SiO J = $8 \rightarrow 7$, and HCN J = $5 \rightarrow 4$ are presented.

evidence.quote: At a distance of only 77 Mpc, ALMA’s high spatial resolution resolves the emission from the two merging nuclei
At a distance of only 77 Mpc, ALMA’s high spatial resolution resolves the emission from the two merging nuclei

question.value: What are the morphology, kinematics, outflows and physical conditions (temperature, optical depth, mass) of the Arp 220 nuclear disks and extended gas, as probed by CO, 13CO, HCN and SiO and non-LTE LIME models?

evidence.quote: These observations are compared to non-LTE radiative transfer models created using the Line Modeling Engine (LIME) for simple gas dynamics
ALMA’s band 7 receivers on August 17$^{th}$ of 2016 (Project 2015.1.00736.S) during cycle-3
Arp 220 was observed in $^{13}$CO J = $4 \rightarrow 3$ with ALMA’s band 8 receivers

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Band 7: 350.6, 352.4 (continuum), 340.6 (12CO), 342.4 GHz (SiO); Band 8: 432.0 (13CO), 433.8 (HCN/continuum), 421.8 GHz; 15.625 MHz resolution TDM

evidence.quote: The bands observed were centered on 432.0 GHz ($^{13}$CO J = $4 \rightarrow 3$), 433.8 GHz (HCN J = $5 \rightarrow 4$/continuum), and 421.8 GHz (continuum).
ALMA cycle 3 observations of $^{12}$CO $J = 3\rightarrow2$
$^{13}$CO $J =  4\rightarrow 3$
SiO J = $8 \rightarrow 7$
HCN J = $5 \rightarrow 4$
in a configuration with baselines ranging from 15 m to 1.4 km

angular_resolution.value: Band 7 beam 0.244" x 0.175"; Band 8 beam 0.177" x 0.125"

evidence.quote: The beam size was 0.244" x 0.175" with a position angle of 0.34$^\circ$.

sensitivity.value: ~1.5 mJy/beam (Band 7) and ~1.1 mJy/beam (Band 8) per 20 km/s channel

evidence.quote: The 1 $\sigma$ noise in a cleaned 20 km/s spectral channel is $\sim$1.1 mJy/beam.
The total on-source integration time was 102 minutes using 51 antennas.

observing_dates.value: Band 7: 17 Aug 2016; Band 8: 29-30 Jul and 17-18 Aug 2016

evidence.quote: on July 29$^{th}$ and 30$^{th}$ of 2016 as well as on August 17$^{th}$ and 18$^{th}$ of 2016

what.value: CO J=1-0 data re-imaged with robust 0.5 and 20 km/s channels; line fluxes 47.3 and 27.8 Jy km/s used for scaling

evidence.quote: The $^{12}$CO J = $1 \rightarrow 0$ data are that of (cite: Scoville2017), but imaged with robust = 0.5 rather than 1

what.value: CO to H2 conversion factor 0.8 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1

evidence.quote: using the conversion factor 0.8 M$_\odot$ (K km/s pc$^2$)$^{-1}$ (cite: DownesSolomon1998)
Using the $L_{FIR}$ measured from the ALMA 691 GHz continuum emission from (cite: Wilson2014).
The default dust opacity values of LIME were used in the models, which are from (cite: Ossenkopf1994).

pipeline_or_manual.value: Calibrated and imaged by ALMA staff; delivered products used without additional processing

evidence.quote: The delivered observations were found to be of high quality and are thus presented here without additional processing.
The observations were flagged, calibrated, and imaged by ALMA staff prior to delivery.
Imaging and cleaning were carried out using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package CASA (cite: CASA).
The observations were imaged using Briggs weighting, with robust set to 0.5
Both observation sets were continuum subtracted using CASA’s uvcontsub routine.
All observations have been corrected for primary beam attenuation.

what.value: Disk axis of 17 deg for western nucleus taken from high-resolution CO 1-0 observations

evidence.quote: 17$^\circ$ is the deconvolved axis derived from the high spatial resolution observations from (cite: Scoville2017).
To simulate the absorption, the approach from (cite: Rangwala2015) was used.

unstated_but_needed: Channel/velocity ranges used for continuum fitting and line-free channels in uvcontsub/imcontsub
Image size, cell size, clean threshold, masks, deconvolver
Exact velocity ranges for the outflow moment maps and HCN/other moments
LIME setup: number of grid points, collision rate files, model image pixel size, band velocity resolution
Distance source and inclination/PA for east disk (45 deg axis) justification

method.value: Use ALMA-delivered products; uvcontsub (imcontsub for model comparison); Briggs robust 0.5; 20 km/s channels

evidence.quote: The observations were imaged using Briggs weighting, with robust set to 0.5

validation.value: uvcontsub and imcontsub give same line profiles within noise

evidence.quote: it was confirmed that the two routines produce the same line profiles within the noise levels of the observations

analysis_steps.goal: Moment maps and Gaussian fits of nuclei

method.value: Moments 1 and 2 from pixels above 4x rms; Gaussian fits to continuum and line maps

evidence.quote: Moments 1 and 2 were constructed utilizing only pixels with a signal greater than 4 times the rms of pixels without signal.
A systemic velocity of 5338 km/s is assumed for moment 1.

analysis_steps.goal: Outflow masses and mass loss rates

method.value: Moment 0 of high-velocity red/blue gas; L'CO from Solomon 1992 equation; scale 3-2 to 1-0 using nuclear luminosity ratio; mass with alpha=0.8; age = corrected size / corrected velocity

evidence.quote: an age is calculated by dividing the corrected size by the corrected velocity

assumptions.value: CO-to-H2 factor 0.8 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1; inclination from LIME models

evidence.quote: using the conversion factor 0.8 M$_\odot$ (K km/s pc$^2$)$^{-1}$
The sizes of the outflow were fit using CASA and are shown in Table [2](#out_table).

analysis_steps.goal: Non-LTE LIME disk modeling of nuclei

method.value: Exponential disk density profile with uniform gas/dust temperature and turbulence, CO/H2 = 2e-4; model images convolved with beam, imcontsub, spectra compared at half-beam increments; parameters adjusted by eye

evidence.quote: The spectra are extracted from the model images and the observations at half-beam increments along the plane of the disk as well as orthogonal to it

key_parameters.value: Continuum integrated intensity in model matched to observations

evidence.quote: the integrated intensity in the continuum map that is produced is required to be the same as that measured in the observations
Abundance of $^{12}$CO to $^{13}$CO$^a$

fitting.value: No statistical fitting; ranges by eye

evidence.quote: although no statistical fitting was carried out

validation.value: Column densities compared with literature values

evidence.quote: The agreement with these other values in the literature help validate this model against other physical measurements of Arp 220 east.

used_for.value: Imaging, continuum subtraction, beam convolution, moment maps, Gaussian fits

evidence.quote: Imaging and cleaning were carried out using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package CASA (cite: CASA).
LIME, the Line Modeling Engine (cite: Brinch2010), is a non-LTE spectral line radiation transfer code for 3D models in arbitrary geometries
a mass of 2.0$\times$10$^7$ M$_\odot$ for the red outflow and 2.0$\times$10$^6$ M$_\odot$ for the blue outflow in the western nucleus

This yields a mass of 5$\times$10$^6$ M$_\odot$ and 4$\times$10$^6$ M$_\odot$ for the red and blue outflows respectively.
$8 \cdot 10^8$, M$_\odot$

findings_qualitative.value: Extended 12CO 3-2 emission shows m=2 tidal-like features suggesting gas inflow

evidence.quote: morphology that is indicative of m = 2 tidal features, suggesting gas inflow

claims.hypothesis: Is the eastern nucleus line asymmetry caused by a foreground absorber, outflow, or temperature asymmetry?
claims.experiment: LIME models of 12CO and 13CO line profiles at multiple positions
claims.result: Absorber fails for 13CO; outflow fails off-axis; asymmetric temperature disk fits best
claims.finding: Temperature asymmetry best explains the eastern nucleus

evidence.quote: The eastern nucleus is found to be best modeled with an inclusion of a temperature asymmetry from one side of the disk to the other.

claims.hypothesis: Is the western nucleus optically thick even in 13CO?
claims.experiment: LIME model optical depth map and central absorption
claims.result: Peak tau 18 with dust; central dip below zero
claims.finding: 13CO 4-3 is optically thick and absorbs continuum

evidence.quote: the western nucleus is optically thick even in the less abundant species of $^{13}$CO, absorbing significant amounts of continuum radiation.

claims.hypothesis: Are outflows present in both nuclei?
claims.finding: First strong detection of eastern outflow

evidence.quote: outflow for both nuclei are found in the $^{12}$CO J $= 3\rightarrow2$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Foreground absorber and pure outflow models rejected for the eastern nucleus asymmetry

evidence.quote: Thus, the asymmetric line profiles observed in $^{13}$CO J = $4 \rightarrow 3$ rule out the possibility of a foreground absorber as the cause of the asymmetry.

limitations_admitted.value: No statistical fitting; parameter ranges by eye; degenerate parameters

evidence.quote: A more quantitative treatment was computationally too expensive.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model parameters chosen by eye with no uncertainty or goodness-of-fit estimate
Red outflow mass contaminated by H13CN
Only 4 minutes of Band 7 on-source time

reproducibility.score_reason: Archival ALMA data with clear imaging basics, but LIME modeling is by-eye and scripts/parameters are incomplete.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main modeling results are by-eye and not reproducible without scripts, though flux and moment measurements could be redone.
